chunks: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Ja'far ibn Bashir, from Hammad ibn 'Uthman, from Jamil ibn Salih, from 'Abdullah ibn 'Amr, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about al-Mut'ah, and he said: 'It is permissible by Allah and His Messenger.' I said: 'What is its limit/condition?' He said: 'Among its conditions is that she does not inherit you, nor do you inherit her.' I said: 'What is her waiting period (Iddah)?' He said: 'Forty-five days, or three pure menstrual cycles.'
ai.seo_question: What are the conditions and waiting period for temporary marriage (Mut'ah) in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this narration from al-Istibsar, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the legal boundaries of al-Mut'ah, emphasizing that while it is a valid contract, it inherently excludes mutual inheritance unless explicitly stipulated. The specification of the Iddah as either forty-five days or three complete menstrual cycles provides a practical framework for determining the end of the temporary union, reflecting the juristic flexibility within Shia fiqh regarding temporal versus biological markers of duration.
